newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait Central Bank wants shift to Islam economy.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Central Bank wants shift to Islam economy.

text.p: Kuwait's Central Bank governor Sheikh Salem Abdul-Aziz al-Sabah said shifting to Islamic economy is a strategic goal, the official Kuwait News Agency reported on Monday.
"Shifting to Islamic economy represents a strategic goal that we hope would be achieved in the future," the agency quoted Sheikh Salem as saying in an interview.

"Constant growth in the volume and number of Islamic finance institutions represents a commendable trend to develop the economies of the Islamic countries and to prepare the atmosphere for compliance with the rules of Islamic Sharia (teachings)," said Sheikh Salem. He did not elaborate.
A key tool of Islamic banking is Murabaha -- a method designed to avert interest payments where financial institutions buy goods upon agreement with a client and sell them on to him at a profit.
Efforts by the bank to draft a law that would regulate the operations of Islamic banks are in progress, he said.

The envisaged law would place Islamic banks under the supervision of the central bank, bankers say. Currently firms with banking activities are not required by law to adhere to the central bank's regulations.

Sheikh Salem, who has said Kuwait has what he called an oversufficiency of traditional commercial banks relative to the number of customers, said he did not object to the principle of creating more Islamic banking units in Kuwait.
But the central bank should have a say in their creation.

Sheikh Salem said he rejects the idea of traditional banks starting Islamic banking services. "It is not correct -- from auditing viewpoint or in terms of compliance with the rules of the Islamic Sharia -- that a banking unit practises an Islamic banking activity along with a traditional banking activity at the same time."
Kuwait has six commercial banks, two specialised banks, an Islamic finance institution with retail banking activities and a branch of a foreign bank.
